name: Voxel Raytracer
body: A voxel raytracer renders 3D voxel models by marching rays through a 3D grid of voxels, supporting multiple bounces for diffuse reflection and a ground plane. It differs from standard voxel grid raycasting by implementing a full path-tracing loop with diffuse scattering and anti-aliasing, rather than simple direct illumination or single-pass raymarching. Inputs: A 1D array of vec4 (RGBA) representing the voxel grid, stored in row-major order (x, then y, then z). Model metadata: position (vec3) and size (ivec3) for each model in the scene. Camera parameters: resolution (iResolution), number of models, and maximum depth. Outputs: A final color image with gamma correction applied. VoxelModel: position: vec3 (world position of the model). size: ivec3 (dimensions of the voxel grid in voxels). HitRecord: p: vec3 (hit point in world space). t: float (distance from ray origin to hit point). normal: vec3 (surface normal at hit point). albedo: vec3 (diffuse color at hit point). Storage Buffer Object (SSBO): A single array of vec4 bound to binding point 0. Index calculation for voxel (x, y, z) in a model of size (width, height, length): \text{index} = (x + y \cdot \text{width} + z \cdot \text{width} \cdot \text{height}) \cdot 4 This index points to the start of the 4 float components (RGBA) in the flat array. SAMPLESPERPIXEL: 256. MAXDEPTH: 50. MAXMODELS: 10. 1. Random Number Generation: Initialize a PCG state per pixel using iResolution.x glFragCoord.y + glFragCoord.x. The stepRandom function updates state: rngState 747796405 + 1. The random function permutes the state: word = ((rngState >> ((rngState >> 28) + 4)) ^ rngState) 277803737; word = (word >> 22) ^ word; and returns float(word) / 4294967295.0f. 2. Voxel Presence Check: For a given voxel coordinate voxOrigin, check bounds 0 <= x < modelSize.x, 0 <= y < modelSize.y, 0 <= z < modelSize.z. If out of bounds, return false. Otherwise, access data[voxOrigin.x + voxOrigin.y modelSize.x + voxOrigin.z modelSize.x modelSize.y]. Extract albedo from.xyz. Return true if alpha.a > 0. 3. Voxel Marching (DDA): 1. Initialize voxOrigin = ivec3(floor(ray.origin)). 2. Calculate step direction: posStepDir = ivec3(step(0.0, ray.direction)), stepDir = ivec3(posStepDir 2 - 1). 3. Calculate justOut coordinates for boundary exit: posStepDir (models[0].size - 1) + stepDir. 4. Calculate initial tMax: (posStepDir - (ray.origin - voxOrigin)) / ray.direction. 5. Calculate tDelta: stepDir / ray.direction. 6. Loop up to 1000 times: a. Check voxelPresent(voxOrigin). If present, set rec.normal = lastOrigin - voxOrigin, rec.t = tMin, rec.p = ray.origin + tMin ray.direction, return true. b. Update lastOrigin = voxOrigin. c. Compare tMax components to determine which axis to step. d. Increment voxOrigin on that axis. e. If voxOrigin equals justOut on that axis, break loop. f. Update tMin to the tMax of the stepped axis. g. Update tMax for that axis by adding tDelta. 4. Ground Hit: Calculate intersection with plane y=0: t = (0 - ray.origin.y) / ray.direction.y. If t < 0 or t > 50, return false. Set normal: vec3(0.0, float(ray.direction.y < 0) 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0). Set albedo to (0.8, 0.8, 0.0). Set p = ray.origin + ray.direction t. Return true. 5. World Hit: Call groundHit and voxelMarch. If both hit, return the one with smaller t. If only one hits, return that one. If neither, return false. 6. Ray Generation: Camera center is at (models[0].size.x / 2, models[0].size.y / 2, models[0].size.z + 12). Viewport height is 2.0. Viewport width is 2.0 imagewidth / imageheight. Viewport lower left is center - vec3(0, 0, 1.0) - viewportu / 2 - viewportv / 2. Pixel 0,0 location is viewportlowerleft + 0.5 (pixeldeltau + pixeldeltav). Ray direction is normalized vector from center to pixel00loc + (glFragCoord.x - 0.5 + random()) pixeldeltau + (glFragCoord.y - 0.5 + random()) pixeldeltav. 7. Color Calculation (Path Tracing): Initialize outcolor = (1,1,1). Loop d from 0 to MAXDEPTH-1. Generate ray using getray(). Call worldHit(ray, rec). If hit: calculate scatter direction: rec.normal + randomunitvector(). Handle near-zero scatter direction: if abs(scatterdir.x/y/z) < 1e-8, set scatterdir = rec.normal. Update ray origin: rec.p + scatterdir 0.001. Update ray direction: scatterdir. Multiply outcolor by rec.albedo. If no hit: calculate sky gradient factor a = 0.5 (ray.direction.y + 1.0). Mix white (1,1,1) and sky blue (0.5, 0.7, 1.0) using a. Multiply outcolor by result. Break loop. 8. Final Output: Accumulate SAMPLESPERPIXEL samples. Average by dividing by SAMPLESPERPIXEL. Apply gamma correction by taking the square root. Output as vec4(sqrt(outcolor / SAMPLESPERPIXEL), 1.0). Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math SAMPLESPERPIXEL = 256 MAXDEPTH = 50 MAXMODELS = 10 class VoxelModel: def init(self, position, size): self.position = position # vec3 self.size = size # ivec3 class HitRecord: def init(self): self.p = None # vec3 self.t = None # float self.normal = None # vec3 self.albedo = None # vec3 class Ray: def init(self, origin, direction): self.origin = origin self.direction = direction class PCG: def init(self, state): self.state = state def steprandom(self): self.state = (self.state 747796405 + 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF def random(self): self.steprandom() word = self.state word = ((word >> ((word >> 28) + 4)) ^ word) 277803737 word = (word >> 22) ^ word return float(word) / 4294967295.0 def voxelpresent(data, modelsize, voxorigin): x, y, z = voxorigin if x < 0 or y < 0 or z < 0 or x >= modelsize[0] or y >= modelsize[1] or z >= modelsize[2]: return False, None width, height, length = modelsize index = (x + y width + z width height) 4 r = data[index] g = data[index + 1] b = data[index + 2] a = data[index + 3] if a > 0: return True, (r, g, b) return False, None def voxelmarch(ray, data, modelsize): voxorigin = (int(math.floor(ray.origin[0])), int(math.floor(ray.origin[1])), int(math.floor(ray.origin[2]))) posstepdir = (1 if ray.direction[0] >= 0 else 0, 1 if ray.direction[1] >= 0 else 0, 1 if ray.direction[2] >= 0 else 0) stepdir = (posstepdir[0] 2 - 1, posstepdir[1] 2 - 1, posstepdir[2] 2 - 1) justout = (posstepdir[0] (modelsize[0] - 1) + stepdir[0], posstepdir[1] (modelsize[1] - 1) + stepdir[1], posstepdir[2] (modelsize[2] - 1) + stepdir[2]) tmax = ((posstepdir[0] - (ray.origin[0] - voxorigin[0])) / ray.direction[0], (posstepdir[1] - (ray.origin[1] - voxorigin[1])) / ray.direction[1], (posstepdir[2] - (ray.origin[2] - voxorigin[2])) / ray.direction[2]) tdelta = (stepdir[0] / ray.direction[0], stepdir[1] / ray.direction[1], stepdir[2] / ray.direction[2]) lastorigin = voxorigin tmin = 0 for in range(1000): present, albedo = voxelpresent(data, modelsize, voxorigin) if present: rec = HitRecord() rec.normal = (lastorigin[0] - voxorigin[0], lastorigin[1] - voxorigin[1], lastorigin[2] - voxorigin[2]) rec.t = tmin rec.p = (ray.origin[0] + tmin ray.direction[0], ray.origin[1] + tmin ray.direction[1], ray.origin[2] + tmin ray.direction[2]) rec.albedo = albedo return rec lastorigin = voxorigin if tmax[0] < tmax[1]: if tmax[0] < tmax[2]: voxorigin = (voxorigin[0] + stepdir[0], voxorigin[1], voxorigin[2]) if voxorigin[0] == justout[0]: break tmin = tmax[0] tmax = (tmax[0] + tdelta[0], tmax[1], tmax[2]) else: voxorigin = (voxorigin[0], voxorigin[1], voxorigin[2] + stepdir[2]) if voxorigin[2] == justout[2]: break tmin = tmax[2] tmax = (tmax[0], tmax[1], tmax[2] + tdelta[2]) else: if tmax[1] < tmax[2]: voxorigin = (voxorigin[0], voxorigin[1] + stepdir[1], voxorigin[2]) if voxorigin[1] == justout[1]: break tmin = tmax[1] tmax = (tmax[0], tmax[1] + tdelta[1], tmax[2]) else: voxorigin = (voxorigin[0], voxorigin[1], voxorigin[2] + stepdir[2]) if voxorigin[2] == justout[2]: break tmin = tmax[2] tmax = (tmax[0], tmax[1], tmax[2] + tdelta[2]) return None def groundhit(ray): if ray.direction[1] == 0: return None t = (0 - ray.origin[1]) / ray.direction[1] if t < 0 or t > 50: return None rec = HitRecord() rec.normal = (0.0, 1.0 if ray.direction[1] < 0 else -1.0, 0.0) rec.t = t rec.albedo = (0.8, 0.8, 0.0) rec.p = (ray.origin[0] + ray.direction[0] t, ray.origin[1] + ray.direction[1] t, ray.origin[2] + ray.direction[2] t) return rec def worldhit(ray, data, modelsize): groundrec = groundhit(ray) voxrec = voxelmarch(ray, data, modelsize) if groundrec and voxrec: if groundrec.t < voxrec.t: return groundrec else: return voxrec elif groundrec: return groundrec elif voxrec: return voxrec else: return None def randominunitsphere(rng): while True: p = (rng.random() 2 - 1, rng.random() 2 - 1, rng.random() 2 - 1) if p[0]2 + p[1]2 + p[2]2 < 1: return p def randomunitvector(rng): p = randominunitsphere(rng) length = math.sqrt(p[0]2 + p[1]2 + p[2]2) return (p[0]/length, p[1]/length, p[2]/length) def getray(rng, fx, fy, modelsize, resolution): imagewidth, imageheight = resolution aspectratio = imagewidth / imageheight center = (modelsize[0] / 2, modelsize[1] / 2, modelsize[2] + 12) viewportheight = 2.0 viewportwidth = viewportheight imagewidth / imageheight viewportu = (viewportwidth, 0.0, 0.0) viewportv = (0.0, viewportheight, 0.0) pixeldeltau = (viewportu[0] / imagewidth, viewportu[1] / imagewidth, viewportu[2] / imagewidth) pixeldeltav = (viewportv[0] / imageheight, viewportv[1] / imageheight, viewportv[2] / imageheight) viewportlowerleft = (center[0] - 0.0 - viewportu[0]/2 - viewportv[0]/2, center[1] - 0.0 - viewportu[1]/2 - viewportv[1]/2, center[2] - 1.0 - viewportu[2]/2 - viewportv[2]/2) pixel00loc = (viewportlowerleft[0] + 0.5 (pixeldeltau[0] + pixeldeltav[0]), viewportlowerleft[1] + 0.5 (pixeldeltau[1] + pixeldeltav[1]), viewportlowerleft[2] + 0.5 (pixeldeltau[2] + pixeldeltav[2])) pixeloffset = ( (fx - 0.5 + rng.random()) pixeldeltau[0] + (fy - 0.5 + rng.random()) pixeldeltav[0], (fx - 0.5 + rng.random()) pixeldeltau[1] + (fy - 0.5 + rng.random()) pixeldeltav[1], (fx - 0.5 + rng.random()) pixeldeltau[2] + (fy - 0.5 + rng.random()) pixeldeltav[2]) target = (pixel00loc[0] + pixeloffset[0], pixel00loc[1] + pixeloffset[1], pixel00loc[2] + pixeloffset[2]) direction = (target[0] - center[0], target[1] - center[1], target[2] - center[2]) length = math.sqrt(direction[0]2 + direction[1]2 + direction[2]2) direction = (direction[0]/length, direction[1]/length, direction[2]/length) return Ray(center, direction) def getcolor(fx, fy, rng, data, modelsize, resolution): outcolor = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) for in range(SAMPLESPERPIXEL): ray = getray(rng, fx, fy, modelsize, resolution) for d in range(MAXDEPTH): rec = worldhit(ray, data, modelsize) if rec: scatterdir = (rec.normal[0] + randomunitvector(rng)[0], rec.normal[1] + randomunitvector(rng)[1], rec.normal[2] + randomunitvector(rng)[2]) if abs(scatterdir[0]) < 1e-8 and abs(scatterdir[1]) < 1e-8 and abs(scatterdir[2]) < 1e-8: scatterdir = rec.normal ray.origin = (rec.p[0] + scatterdir[0] 0.001, rec.p[1] + scatterdir[1] 0.001, rec.p[2] + scatterdir[2] 0.001) length = math.sqrt(scatterdir[0]2 + scatterdir[1]2 + scatterdir[2]2) ray.direction = (scatterdir[0]/length, scatterdir[1]/length, scatterdir[2]/length) outcolor = (outcolor[0] rec.albedo[0], outcolor[1] rec.albedo[1], outcolor[2] rec.albedo[2]) else: a = 0.5 (ray.direction[1] + 1.0) sky = (1.0 - a) (1.0, 1.0, 1.0) + a (0.5, 0.7, 1.0) outcolor = (outcolor[0] sky[0], outcolor[1] sky[1], outcolor[2] sky[2]) break return (math.sqrt(outcolor[0] / SAMPLESPERPIXEL), math.sqrt(outcolor[1] / SAMPLESPERPIXEL), math.sqrt(outcolor[2] / SAMPLESPERPIXEL)) Precision: The DDA uses floating-point arithmetic for tMax and tDelta. The loop limit of 1000 iterations prevents infinite loops. Boundaries: The voxelPresent function explicitly checks bounds to avoid out-of-bounds memory access. Degenerate Rays: If ray.direction.y is 0 in groundHit, division by zero occurs. The source does not explicitly handle this, but t would be infinity or NaN, likely failing the t < 0 check if handled correctly, or causing undefined behavior. Scatter Direction Zero: If the random vector cancels the normal exactly, the scatter direction becomes zero. The code checks for this and resets to the normal. Time Complexity: O(N \cdot S \cdot D \cdot V), where N is the number of pixels, S is samples per pixel, D is max depth, and V is the number of voxels traversed per ray. Memory Complexity: O(W \cdot H \cdot L) for the voxel grid storage, where W, H, L are the dimensions of the voxel model. Measured Performance: Rendered on a GTX 1050 TI Mobile with 256 samples per pixel and 50 max bounces. Times: 82.95 ms, 74.47 ms, 516.46 ms for different scenes. Strengths: Simple implementation, supports diffuse reflections, anti-aliasing, and soft shadows (via multiple bounces). Limitations: No explicit acceleration structure (like an octree) is used for the voxel grid itself, relying on DDA which can be slow for large empty spaces. No support for specular materials or complex lighting. The method is based on an unofficial voxel raytracer implementation by ahmedkhalf. It builds on standard ray tracing techniques, specifically DDA for voxel traversal, and path tracing for global illumination. The random number generation uses a PCG algorithm commonly found in graphics programming. ahmedkhalf/voxel-raytracer, https://github.com/ahmedkhalf/voxel-raytracer, fetched 2026-10-24 (unofficial)

name: DirectVoxGO Volume Rendering
head: DirectVoxGO, Voxel Grid Neural Rendering
body: DirectVoxGO is a volume rendering method that accelerates neural radiance field training and inference by sampling points directly on a structured voxel grid rather than uniformly along rays. It solves the problem of inefficient ray marching in sparse scenes by using a mask cache to skip free space and a direct lookup of density and color features from the voxel grid. It sets itself apart from standard NeRF by replacing uniform sampling with grid-based point selection and from other sparse voxel methods by using a dense voxel grid with a binary mask cache for acceleration. Inputs and Outputs: Inputs: Ray origins rayso ([N, 3]), ray directions raysd ([N, 3]), view directions viewdirs ([N, 3]), near/far distances, and rendering parameters. Outputs: Rendered RGB images rgbmarched ([N, 3]), accumulated transmittance alphainvlast ([N]), and intermediate weights weights ([M]). Data Structures: Voxel Grid: A 3D tensor storing density and color features, defined by xyzmin and xyzmax bounding boxes and a resolution numvoxels. Mask Cache: A binary tensor indicating which voxels contain geometry (true) or are free space (false). Ray Points: raypts ([M, 3]) stores the 3D coordinates of sampled points. rayid ([M]) maps each point to its originating ray. stepid ([M]) maps each point to its step index along the ray. Parameters: stepsize: Number of voxels per sample step. fastcolorthres: Threshold for filtering points based on alpha or weight values; if > 0, enables optimization. voxelsizeratio: Ratio used to compute interval for density-to-alpha conversion. rgbnetdirect: Boolean flag determining if the RGB network outputs direct RGB or residual features. Steps: 1. Ray Setup: Compute ray origins and directions from camera parameters. If NDC (Normalized Device Coordinates) is enabled, transform rays to NDC space. Ray direction computation (for inversey=False, flipy=False, mode='center'): \text{dirs} = \left[ \frac{i - K{0,2}}{K{0,0}}, \frac{j - K{1,2}}{K{1,1}}, 1 \right] NDC ray transformation: o0 = -\frac{1}{W/(2 \cdot \text{focal})} \frac{ox}{oz}, \quad d0 = -\frac{1}{W/(2 \cdot \text{focal})} \left(\frac{dx}{dz} - \frac{ox}{oz}\right) 2. Sample Points: Calculate step distance stepdist = stepsize voxelsize. Sample points along rays within the bounding box [xyzmin, xyzmax]. Filter points outside the bounding box. Input: rayso, raysd, near, far, stepdist. Output: raypts, rayid, stepid, maskoutbbox. 3. Free Space Culling: Query the mask cache for the sampled points. Filter out points where the mask is false (free space). 4. Density Query: Query the voxel grid for density values at the remaining points. 5. Alpha Conversion: Convert density to alpha using the Raw2Alpha function: \alpha = 1 - (1 + \exp(\text{density} + \text{shift}))^{-\text{interval}} where interval = stepsize voxelsizeratio. 6. First Color Threshold: If fastcolorthres > 0, filter points where alpha > fastcolorthres. 7. Weight Computation: Compute accumulated transmittance and weights using Alphas2Weights.apply(alpha, rayid, N). This function performs a segmented sum over rays to compute weights and the final transmittance alphainvlast. 8. Second Color Threshold: If fastcolorthres > 0, filter points where weights > fastcolorthres. 9. Color Query: Query the voxel grid for color features k0 at the remaining points. 10. RGB Computation: If rgbnet is None: rgb = sigmoid(k0). If rgbnet is not None: If rgbnetdirect: rgbfeat = k0. Else: k0view = k0[:, 3:], k0diffuse = k0[:,:3]. Compute view direction embeddings: viewdirsemb = (viewdirs.unsqueeze(-1) viewfreq).flatten(-2), then concatenate with sin/cos of viewdirs. rgbfeat = cat([k0view, viewdirsemb], -1). rgblogit = rgbnet(rgbfeat). If rgbnetdirect: rgb = sigmoid(rgblogit). Else: rgb = sigmoid(rgblogit + k0diffuse). 11. Accumulation: Accumulate RGB using segmented sum: \text{rgb\marched} = \sum{i \in \text{ray}} \text{weights}i \cdot \text{rgb}i Add background color: rgbmarched += alphainvlast bg. o) / d tnear = torch.max(torch.min(t1, t2)) tfar = torch.min(torch.max(t1, t2)) tnear = torch.max(tnear, torch.tensor(near)) tfar = torch.min(tfar, torch.tensor(far)) if tnear >= tfar: maskoutbbox.append(torch.ones(maxsteps, dtype=bool)) continue tmin[i] = tnear tmax[i] = tfar numsteps = int((tfar - tnear) / stepdist) + 1 ts = torch.arange(numsteps) stepdist + tnear pts = o.unsqueeze(0) + ts.unsqueeze(1) d.unsqueeze(0) raypts.append(pts) rayid.append(torch.full((numsteps,), i)) stepid.append(torch.arange(numsteps)) maskoutbbox.append(torch.zeros(numsteps, dtype=bool)) raypts = torch.cat(raypts, dim=0) if raypts else torch.empty(0, 3) rayid = torch.cat(rayid, dim=0) if rayid else torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.long) stepid = torch.cat(stepid, dim=0) if stepid else torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.long) maskoutbbox = torch.cat(maskoutbbox, dim=0) if maskoutbbox else torch.empty(0, dtype=bool) Nsteps = maxsteps return raypts, maskoutbbox, rayid, stepid, Nsteps, tmin, tmax def alphas2weights(alpha, rayid, N): M = alpha.shape[0] weights = torch.zeros(M, dtype=alpha.dtype) alphainvlast = torch.zeros(N, dtype=alpha.dtype) rayindices = [[] for in range(N)] for i, rid in enumerate(rayid): if rid < N: rayindices[rid].append(i) for r in range(N): if not rayindices[r]: continue Tcurr = 1.0 for idx in rayindices[r]: a = alpha[idx].item() weights[idx] = Tcurr a Tcurr = (1.0 - a) alphainvlast[r] = 1.0 - Tcurr return weights, alphainvlast def segmentcoo(src, index, out, reduce='sum'): for i in range(src.shape[0]): r = index[i].item() if r < out.shape[0]: if reduce == 'sum': out[r] += src[i] return out def renderdirectvoxgo(rayso, raysd, viewdirs, model, renderkwargs): stepdist = renderkwargs['stepsize'] model.voxelsize raypts, maskoutbbox, rayid, stepid, Nsteps, tmin, tmax = sampleptsonrays( rayso, raysd, model.xyzmin, model.xyzmax, renderkwargs['near'], renderkwargs['far'], stepdist) maskinbbox = ~maskoutbbox raypts = raypts[maskinbbox] rayid = rayid[maskinbbox] stepid = stepid[maskinbbox] if model.maskcache is not None: mask = model.maskcache(raypts) raypts = raypts[mask] rayid = rayid[mask] stepid = stepid[mask] density = model.density(raypts) interval = renderkwargs['stepsize'] model.voxelsizeratio alpha = 1.0 - (1.0 + torch.exp(density + model.shift)) (-interval) if model.fastcolorthres > 0: mask = (alpha > model.fastcolorthres) raypts = raypts[mask] rayid = rayid[mask] stepid = stepid[mask] density = density[mask] alpha = alpha[mask] weights, alphainvlast = alphas2weights(alpha, rayid, len(rayso)) if model.fastcolorthres > 0: mask = (weights > model.fastcolorthres) weights = weights[mask] alpha = alpha[mask] raypts = raypts[mask] rayid = rayid[mask] stepid = stepid[mask] k0 = model.k0(raypts) if model.rgbnet is None: rgb = torch.sigmoid(k0) else: if model.rgbnetdirect: k0view = k0 else: k0view = k0[:, 3:] k0diffuse = k0[:,:3] viewdirsemb = (viewdirs.unsqueeze(-1) model.viewfreq).flatten(-2) viewdirsemb = torch.cat([viewdirs, viewdirsemb.sin(), viewdirsemb.cos()], -1) viewdirsemb = viewdirsemb.flatten(0, -2)[rayid] rgbfeat = torch.cat([k0view, viewdirsemb], -1) rgblogit = model.rgbnet(rgbfeat) if model.rgbnetdirect: rgb = torch.sigmoid(rgblogit) else: rgb = torch.sigmoid(rgblogit + k0diffuse) rgbmarched = segmentcoo( src=(weights.unsqueeze(-1) rgb), index=rayid, out=torch.zeros((len(rayso), 3), dtype=rgb.dtype), reduce='sum') rgbmarched += (alphainvlast.unsqueeze(-1) renderkwargs['bg']) return rgbmarched, alphainvlast Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Far Distance: The far distance can be too small, causing rays to stop prematurely when hitting the scene bounding box. The code sets far = 1e9 to prevent this. View Directions: View directions are passed as input and must be normalized for view-dependent color computation. Time Complexity: Depends on the number of sampled points and the efficiency of the mask cache. The mask cache significantly reduces the number of points processed in free space. Memory Complexity: Proportional to the voxel grid size and the number of rays. The mask cache adds a small memory overhead. Measured Performance: Not given in the sources. Scaling: Scales with the resolution of the voxel grid and the number of rays. Strengths: Efficient sampling in sparse scenes due to free space culling. Direct lookup of features from the voxel grid. Limitations: Requires a predefined bounding box. Performance may degrade in very dense scenes if the mask cache is less effective. When to Use: Suitable for scenes with significant free space and where efficient sampling is critical. When Not to Use: Not suitable for scenes without a clear bounding box or where high-frequency details require very fine voxel grids. The method is implemented in the DirectVoxGO repository. It builds on the idea of using voxel grids for neural rendering, aiming to improve efficiency over standard NeRF by leveraging spatial acceleration structures. name: Voxel Grid Accelerated Ray-Point Intersection
head: GPU voxel grid for ray casting, Pointersect voxel structure
body: This method accelerates the identification of the k nearest points within a cylinder of radius \delta around a query ray in a point cloud, specifically optimized for parallel GPU execution and dynamic scenes where the point cloud changes frequently. Unlike static acceleration structures such as octrees, which require O(n \log n) construction time, this voxel grid approach achieves O(n) construction, making it superior for inverse rendering and dynamic scenarios where the structure must be rebuilt every iteration. Inputs: Point cloud P containing n points. Query ray r = (ro, rd), where ro is the origin and rd is the direction. Parameters: k: Number of nearest points to retrieve. \delta: Radius of the cylinder around the query ray. g: Number of grid cells per dimension in the voxel grid. Outputs: A list of k points from P that are closest to the ray r in terms of perpendicular distance, restricted to those within distance \delta. Data Structures: Voxel Grid: A uniform 3D grid with g^3 cells. Each cell stores a list (or linked list) of point indices belonging to that voxel. Point Table: An array of size n storing the 3D coordinates of each point in P. Steps: 1. Grid Construction: Divide the 3D space containing P into a uniform voxel grid with g cells per dimension. Iterate through all n points in P and assign each point to its corresponding voxel in the grid table. This step takes O(n) operations. 2. Ray Traversal: For each query ray, trace it through the voxel grid to identify candidate voxels intersected by the ray. Compute grid-ray intersection in O(g) time per ray. This computation is parallelized across multiple GPU threads. 3. Candidate Collection: Collect all points located in the intersected voxels. Filter these points to keep only those within perpendicular distance \delta from the ray, resulting in q candidate points. 4. Sorting and Selection: Sort the q candidate points by their perpendicular distance to the ray and select the k nearest ones. Formulas: Time Complexity: The overall time complexity for finding k nearest points within a surrounding cylinder of radius \delta is: O(n + mg + mq \log(q)) where n is the total number of points, m is the number of rays, g is the grid cells per dimension, and q is the number of points lying within the cylinder. Expected Candidates: For uniformly distributed points, the expected number of points in the cylinder is: q = n/g^3 Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def buildvoxelgrid(points, gridsize, boundsmin, boundsmax): """ Builds a uniform voxel grid for a point cloud. points: List of 3D coordinates (n, 3) gridsize: Integer g, number of cells per dimension boundsmin: 3D vector, minimum corner of the grid boundsmax: 3D vector, maximum corner of the grid Returns: A 3D array of lists (gridsize, gridsize, gridsize) """ # Calculate voxel dimensions voxelsize = (boundsmax - boundsmin) / gridsize # Initialize empty grid grid = [[[] for in range(gridsize)] for in range(gridsize)] for z in range(gridsize): for y in range(gridsize): for x in range(gridsize): grid[z][y][x] = [] # Assign points to voxels for point in points: # Calculate voxel coordinates x = int((point[0] - boundsmin[0]) / voxelsize[0]) y = int((point[1] - boundsmin[1]) / voxelsize[1]) z = int((point[2] - boundsmin[2]) / voxelsize[2]) # Clamp to grid boundaries x = max(0, min(x, gridsize - 1)) y = max(0, min(y, gridsize - 1)) z = max(0, min(z, gridsize - 1)) grid[z][y][x].append(point) return grid def rayvoxelintersection(rayorigin, raydirection, gridsize, boundsmin, boundsmax): """ Traces a ray through a uniform voxel grid to find intersected voxels. Uses a 3D DDA (Digital Differential Analyzer) approach. """ # Calculate voxel size voxelsize = (boundsmax - boundsmin) / gridsize # Initialize traversal variables # Current voxel coordinates x, y, z = int((rayorigin[0] - boundsmin[0]) / voxelsize[0]), \ int((rayorigin[1] - boundsmin[1]) / voxelsize[1]), \ int((rayorigin[2] - boundsmin[2]) / voxelsize[2]) # Step directions stepx = 1 if raydirection[0] > 0 else -1 stepy = 1 if raydirection[1] > 0 else -1 stepz = 1 if raydirection[2] > 0 else -1 # Distance to next voxel boundary tmaxx = ((x + (1 if stepx > 0 else 0)) voxelsize[0] + boundsmin[0] - rayorigin[0]) / raydirection[0] tmaxy = ((y + (1 if stepy > 0 else 0)) voxelsize[1] + boundsmin[1] - rayorigin[1]) / raydirection[1] tmaxz = ((z + (1 if stepz > 0 else 0)) voxelsize[2] + boundsmin[2] - rayorigin[2]) / raydirection[2] # Delta distances between voxel boundaries deltax = voxelsize[0] / abs(raydirection[0]) deltay = voxelsize[1] / abs(raydirection[1]) deltaz = voxelsize[2] / abs(raydirection[2]) intersectedvoxels = [] # Traverse until out of bounds while 0 <= x < gridsize and 0 <= y < gridsize and 0 <= z < gridsize: intersectedvoxels.append((x, y, z)) # Advance to next voxel if tmaxx < tmaxy: if tmaxx < tmaxz: x += stepx tmaxx += deltax else: z += stepz tmaxz += deltaz else: if tmaxy < tmaxz: y += stepy tmaxy += deltay else: z += stepz tmaxz += deltaz return intersectedvoxels def perpendiculardistance(point, rayorigin, raydirection): """ Calculates the perpendicular distance from a point to a ray. """ # Vector from ray origin to point v = point - rayorigin # Project v onto ray direction projlength = dot(v, raydirection) # Projection vector proj = projlength raydirection # Perpendicular vector perp = v - proj return length(perp) def findknearestpoints(points, rayorigin, raydirection, k, delta): """ Finds k nearest points to a ray within distance delta. """ candidates = [] for point in points: dist = perpendiculardistance(point, rayorigin, raydirection) if dist <= delta: candidates.append((dist, point)) # Sort by distance candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0]) # Return k nearest return [p for, p in candidates[:k]] def voxelgridraypointintersection(points, rays, gridsize, boundsmin, boundsmax, k, delta): """ Main function combining voxel grid construction and ray-point intersection. """ # Build voxel grid grid = buildvoxelgrid(points, gridsize, boundsmin, boundsmax) results = [] for ray in rays: # Get intersected voxels voxels = rayvoxelintersection(ray.origin, ray.direction, gridsize, boundsmin, boundsmax) # Collect candidates from voxels candidates = [] for (x, y, z) in voxels: for point in grid[z][y][x]: dist = perpendiculardistance(point, ray.origin, ray.direction) if dist <= delta: candidates.append((dist, point)) # Sort and select k nearest candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0]) results.append([p for, p in candidates[:k]]) return results Edge Cases and Pitfalls: The implementation described in the source is not optimized; specifically, retrieving unordered k nearest points from q points can be done in O(q), but the current implementation sorts them, resulting in O(q \log q). For uniformly distributed points, the expected number of points in the cylinder is q = n/g^3. The method is slower than octrees for static scenes but faster to construct, making it suitable for dynamic scenes or inverse rendering where the tree must be rebuilt every iteration. Time Complexity: O(n + mg + mq \log(q)), where n is total points, m is number of rays, g is grid cells per dimension, and q is points within the cylinder. Construction Time: O(n), which is faster than octree construction (O(n \log n)). Query Time: O(g + q \log q) per ray, where g is the cost of grid-ray intersection and q \log q is the cost of sorting candidates. Strengths: Fast construction makes it superior for dynamic scenes or inverse rendering where the point cloud changes frequently and the structure must be rebuilt every iteration. Parallelizable on GPU. Limitations: Slower query performance for static scenes compared to octrees (n \log(n) + m \log(n) + mq). The sorting step is not optimized; using a selection algorithm could reduce the sorting cost to O(q). When to Use: Dynamic scenes, inverse rendering, or scenarios requiring frequent updates to the point cloud structure. When Not to Use: Static scenes where an octree can be built once and reused, as octrees offer faster query performance in that context. The method was introduced in the context of "Pointersect: Neural Rendering with Cloud-Ray Intersection". It was designed to address the inefficiency of rebuilding octrees in dynamic scenes or inverse rendering applications, where many points in the point cloud can change at every iteration. The approach leverages the simplicity and parallelizability of uniform voxel grids to achieve faster construction times compared to hierarchical structures like octrees. name: Cap Node Traversal
head: Cap Node Traversal and Neighbor Finding, Cap intersection, Gargantini and Atkinson Octree Traversal (Cap Node Variant), Neighbor-finding with cap scalars
body: Cap Node Traversal is a specialized ray traversal routine for "cap nodes" in sparse voxel octrees, which are leaf-like structures containing scalar data for a 2 \times 2 \times 2 block of voxels. It solves the problem of efficiently retrieving voxel values and performing isosurface intersection without the overhead of recursive descent into child nodes. It differs from standard interior node traversal by replacing the isovalue range check and recursive child call with direct scalar retrieval and local neighbor finding. Inputs: Ray origin \mathbf{o}, ray direction \mathbf{d}, current cap node C, isovalue I. Outputs: Isosurface intersection point (if any), or traversal continuation. Data Structures: Cap Node (C): Contains a scalar array scalars of size 8. scalars[i]: Scalar value for the i-th voxel in the 2 \times 2 \times 2 block, where i \in [0, 7]. The index i corresponds to the child octant index in the parent octree structure. Steps: 1. Cap Intersection: Perform the standard octree traversal step to determine which of the 8 voxels (octants) the ray intersects within the cap node. Let the intersected child octant index be child \in [0, 7]. 2. Voxel Value Retrieval: Determine the scalar values of the 8 voxels composing the cell. These are stored directly in C.\text{scalars}[0..7]. 3. Isosurface Check: Check if the isovalue I lies within the minimum and maximum of the 8 voxel values. Let V{min} = \min(C.\text{scalars}[0..7]) and V{max} = \max(C.\text{scalars}[0..7]). If I < V{min} or I > V{max}, no isosurface exists within this cap node. 4. Neighbor Finding: If the isosurface check passes, determine the values of the 8 voxels for isosurface intersection. For the intersected voxel child, identify neighbors within the same cap node. For a desired neighbor direction dir \in [0, 7] from the child octant child: Check if (child \ \& \ dir) == 0. If false (i.e., (child \ \& \ dir) == 0), the neighbor is simply C.\text{scalars}[dir]. If true (i.e., (child \ \& \ dir) \neq 0), proceed with neighbor-finding to retrieve the value from outside the cap node. 5. Isosurface Intersection: Perform isosurface intersection using the 8 voxel values as corners of the cell. This involves solving a cubic polynomial for the ray intersection with the trilinearly interpolated surface. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def capnodetraversal(rayo, rayd, capnode, isovalue): # Step 1: Determine intersected child octant # Standard octree traversal routine returns child index in [0, 7] child = 0 # Step 2: Retrieve scalar values scalars = capnode.scalars # Array of 8 floats # Step 3: Isosurface check minval = min(scalars) maxval = max(scalars) if isovalue < minval or isovalue > maxval: return None # No intersection in this cap node # Step 4: Neighbor finding for the 8 voxels voxelvalues = [] for i in range(8): # The value of voxel i is simply scalars[i] voxelvalues.append(scalars[i]) # Step 5: Isosurface intersection # A step the sources do not give is a comment saying so. return None Parameters: Isovalue: The scalar value defining the isosurface. Typical values depend on the dataset. Cap Node Depth: The depth at which cap nodes are defined. Not given in the sources. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Neighbor Finding: Neighbor finding is only required when the neighbor lies outside the immediate local cap node structure defined by the bitwise check; otherwise, direct array access is used. Degenerate Input: If all 8 voxel values are identical, no isosurface is encountered. A leaf-like structure with homogeneous scalar values. Traversed recursively to the same depth as caps. If a neighborhood of identical voxels is encountered, no isosurface is present. Neighbor-finding is performed at borders. See Scalar Leaves. The standard octree traversal routine that cap node traversal modifies. It involves checking isovalue against min/max ranges and recursively calling child traversal. See Octree Traversal. Time Complexity: O(1) for scalar retrieval and isosurface check within a cap node, assuming the child octant is determined. Neighbor finding may add overhead if neighbors are outside the cap. Memory Complexity: O(1) per cap node, storing 8 scalar values. Strengths: Avoids recursive descent overhead for leaf-like structures. Efficient for datasets with many 2 \times 2 \times 2 homogeneous or near-homogeneous regions. Limitations: Requires specific data structure support for cap nodes. Neighbor finding logic adds complexity. When to Use: When the octree contains many cap nodes and efficient isosurface intersection is required. When Not to Use: When the dataset does not benefit from cap node optimization. Cap Node Traversal was introduced in the context of interactive isosurface ray tracing of large octree volumes. It is part of the Gargantini and Atkinson octree traversal method, specifically the cap node variant. The method was developed to optimize ray traversal for sparse voxel octrees by handling leaf-like structures efficiently. name: Sparse Voxel Ray Marching with AABB Exit Planes
head: NAADF voxel traversal, Sparse Voxel Ray Marching with NAADF, voxel DDA with precomputed exit planes, vxray sparse ray march
body: Sparse Voxel Ray Marching with AABB Exit Planes is a ray traversal algorithm for sparse voxel hierarchies that skips empty space by computing the exit plane of the current empty cell using precomputed Axis-Aligned Distance Fields (AADF). It differs from standard DDA Voxel Grid Raycasting by avoiding per-voxel checks in empty regions, and from pure octree traversal Octree Traversal by using fixed-size hierarchical chunks (chunks, bricks, voxels) with texture-based occupancy masks and distance fields rather than dynamic node pointers. Inputs and Outputs: Input: Ray origin rayorigin, ray direction raydir, grid extent gridext, occupancy textures (chunkmasks, brickmasks, voxelmasks), AADF textures (chunkaadf, brickaadf, voxelaadf). Output: Packed cell info (voxel coordinate and entry axis) or sentinel VXNOCELL if the ray misses or exits the grid. Data Structures: Occupancy Masks: Three Texture3D<uint> (chunkmasks, brickmasks, voxelmasks). Each texel is a uint bitmask. The bit at index masklinearidx(coord) indicates occupancy for a block of voxels. masklinearidx(coord) = local.x + local.y VXMASKEXT + local.z VXMASKEXT VXMASKEXT, where local = coord & (VXMASKEXT - 1). AADF Textures: Three Texture3D<uint> (chunkaadf, brickaadf, voxelaadf). Each texel is a uint packing distances to the nearest occupied voxel in 6 directions (±X, ±Y, ±Z). AADF Packing Layout: Bits 0-4: -X distance, 5-9: +X distance, 10-14: -Y distance, 15-19: +Y distance, 20-24: -Z distance, 25-29: +Z distance. Constants: VXMASKEXT (mask block size), VXBRICKEXT (brick size), VXCHUNKEXT (chunk size), VXNOCELL (sentinel). Numbered Steps: 1. Initialize Ray Inverse: Compute invdir = 1.0 / (raydir + (float3)(raydir == 0.0) 1e-30) to handle zero components. 2. Initial AABB Test: Perform ray-AABB intersection against the entire grid [0, gridext]. If no intersection, return VXNOCELL. Formula: t0 = (p0 - rayorigin) invraydir, t1 = (p1 - rayorigin) invraydir, lo = min(t0, t1), hi = max(t0, t1), tmin = max(max(lo.x, lo.y), max(lo.z, 0.0)), tmax = min(min(hi.x, hi.y), hi.z). Return tmin <= tmax. 3. Initial Position: Calculate starting position start = rayorigin + tmin raydir. Compute initial voxel coordinate ipos = int16t3(floor(start + entrymask sign(raydir) 0.5)) and local position localpos = start - float3(ipos). entrymask determines the entry face to adjust ipos. 4. Determine Initial Axis: Compute entryweights = entrymask abs(raydir). Determine crossedaxis: 1 if entryweights.y > entryweights.x, else 0. Then 2 if entryweights.z > max(entryweights.x, entryweights.y), else unchanged. 5. Loop: a. Bounds Check: If any((uint16t3)ipos >= (uint16t)gridext), return VXNOCELL. b. Hierarchy Check: i. Chunk level: cellext = VXBRICKEXT VXCHUNKEXT, coord = ipos / cellext. Check chunkoccupied(coord). If occupied, return packvoxelcell(ipos, crossedaxis). ii. Brick level: cellext = VXBRICKEXT, coord = ipos / cellext. Check brickoccupied(coord). If occupied, return packvoxelcell(ipos, crossedaxis). iii. Voxel level: cellext = 1, coord = ipos. Check voxeloccupied(coord). If occupied, return packvoxelcell(ipos, crossedaxis). c. AADF Skip: If not occupied, load AADF value for the current level (aadf = chunkaadf.Load(...), brickaadf.Load(...), or voxelaadf.Load(...)) depending on cellext. d. Exit Plane Calculation: Compute exit plane coordinate using aadfexitplane(coord, cellext, aadf, raydir). Formula: shiftx = raydir.x < 0.0 ? 0u: 5u, shifty = raydir.y < 0.0 ? 10u: 15u, shiftz = raydir.z < 0.0 ? 20u: 25u. Extract bounds: bounds.x = (packed >> shiftx) & 31u, etc. Calculate lower = max((coord - bounds) cellext, 0), upper = min((coord + 1 + bounds) cellext, gridext). Return raydir.x < 0.0 ? lower.x: upper.x for each component. e. Distance to Exit: Compute sidedist = (exitplane - float3(ipos) - localpos) invdir. Handle zero ray direction components by setting sidedist component to 3e+38. f. Find Minimum: Find t = min(sidedist.x, min(sidedist.y, sidedist.z)). Determine crossed axis: crossed = step(sidedist, t). Update crossedaxis based on weights of the crossed axes. g. Advance: Compute advanced = localpos + max(t, 0.0001) raydir. Compute new integer position celldelta = int16t3(floor(advanced + crossed sign(raydir) 0.5)). Update ipos += celldelta and localpos = advanced - float3(celldelta). Pseudocode: Unverified code. name: Voxel Ray Traversal (AABB-optimized)
head: Fast Voxel Traversal, VoxelRay3Iterator
body: Voxel Ray Traversal (AABB-optimized) is an iterator that traverses a 3D voxel volume along a ray, returning hits for voxels contained within the volume. It solves the problem of efficiently enumerating voxels by combining a standard 3D DDA traversal with an initial Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) rejection test. What sets it apart from its siblings, such as Octree Traversal or Sparse Voxel Ray Marching with AABB Exit Planes, is its reliance on a flat or chunk-based volume structure where the AABB test serves primarily as a "jump ahead" mechanism to skip empty space before the voxel-by-voxel iteration begins, rather than using hierarchical node structures for traversal. Inputs: ray: A ray defined by origin p (Vec3), direction d (Vec3, normalized), and length (f32). volume: A BoundingVolume3 object containing size (Vec3) and a containspoint method to check voxel occupancy. Outputs: An iterator yielding Ray3hit structs, each containing: distance: f32, the distance along the ray to the voxel entry point. voxel: IVec3, the integer coordinates of the voxel. normal: Option<IVec3>, the normal of the face crossed to enter the voxel (negative step direction). The iterator state maintains the following fields: volume: Reference to the volume being traversed. maxd: f32, the maximum distance the ray can travel. i: IVec3, the current voxel index. step: IVec3, the direction of stepping for each axis (+1 or -1). delta: Vec3, the distance along the ray to cross one voxel in each axis. dist: Vec3, the distance from the current position p to the next voxel boundary in each axis. tmax: Vec3, the distance along the ray to the nearest voxel boundary in each axis. t: f32, the current traveled distance. norm: Option<IVec3>, the normal of the last crossed face. done: bool, flag indicating iteration completion. 1. Initialization and AABB Rejection: Normalize the ray direction: d = \text{normalize}(ray.direction). Initialize traveled distance t = 0.0. Check if the floor of the ray origin p is inside the volume: if \text{volume.containspoint}(\lfloor p \rfloor) is false, perform an AABB test against the chunk bounds using testaabbofchunk(volume, p, d, ray.length). If the AABB test fails (returns None), return a done iterator. If the AABB test succeeds, unwrap the intersection point aabb. Back the origin p off by at least 1 voxel: p = aabb - d \times 2.0. Update the traveled distance: t += \text{length}(p - aabb) - 2.0. 2. Calculate Maximum Distance: Calculate maxd as the minimum of the ray's specified length and the current distance t plus the corner-to-corner length of the volume plus 2.0: \text{max\d} = \min(\text{ray.length}, t + \text{length}(\text{volume.size}) + 2.0) 3. Calculate Starting Voxel and Step Direction: Starting voxel i = \lfloor p \rfloor converted to IVec3. Step direction \text{step} = \text{signum}(d) converted to IVec3. 4. Calculate Delta: For each axis k \in \{x, y, z\}, calculate \deltak: \deltak = \begin{cases} \infty & \text{if } |dk| < \epsilon \\ 1.0 / |dk| & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} where \epsilon = \text{f32::EPSILON}. 5. Calculate Distance to Boundary: For each axis k, calculate \text{dist}k: \text{dist}k = \begin{cases} ik + 1.0 - pk & \text{if } \text{step}k > 0 \\ pk - ik & \text{if } \text{step}k \le 0 \end{cases} 6. Calculate tmax: For each axis k, calculate t{\text{max}, k}: t{\text{max}, k} = \begin{cases} \deltak \times \text{dist}k & \text{if } \deltak < \infty \\ \infty & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} 7. Iteration Loop: While t \le \text{max\d}: Check if the current voxel i is within the volume using \text{volume.containspoint}(i). If true, create a Ray3hit with distance = t, voxel = i, and normal mapped from norm. Select the axis with the smallest t{\text{max}}: If t{\text{max}, x} < t{\text{max}, y} and t{\text{max}, x} < t{\text{max}, z}: ix += \text{step}x t = t{\text{max}, x} t{\text{max}, x} += \deltax \text{norm} = (-\text{step}x, 0, 0) Else if t{\text{max}, y} < t{\text{max}, z}: iy += \text{step}y t = t{\text{max}, y} t{\text{max}, y} += \deltay \text{norm} = (0, -\text{step}y, 0) Else: iz += \text{step}z t = t{\text{max}, z} t{\text{max}, z} += \deltaz \text{norm} = (0, 0, -\text{step}z) If a hit was found in the current voxel, return it immediately. If the loop finishes without finding a hit, set done = true and return None. The testaabbofchunk function calculates the intersection of a ray with an AABB defined by min (Vec3::ZERO) and max (volume.size as Vec3): 1. For each axis i \in \{0, 1, 2\}, calculate ti: ti = \begin{cases} \frac{\text{min}i - \text{from}i}{\text{direction}i} & \text{if } \text{direction}i > 0.0 \\ \frac{\text{max}i - \text{from}i}{\text{direction}i} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} 2. Find the axis mi with the smallest t value using nested comparisons. 3. Validate intersection: If t{mi} \ge 0.0 and t{mi} \le \text{distance}, calculate the intersection point pt = \text{from} + \text{direction} \times t{mi}. 4. Check if the other two dimensions of pt are within [\text{min}, \text{max}]. If so, return pt. Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math from typing import Optional, Tuple class Vec3: def init(self, x: float, y: float, z: float): self.x = x self.y = y self.z = z def normalize(self) -> 'Vec3': length = math.sqrt(self.x2 + self.y2 + self.z2) if length == 0: return Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) return Vec3(self.x / length, self.y / length, self.z / length) def length(self) -> float: return math.sqrt(self.x2 + self.y2 + self.z2) def signum(self) -> 'Vec3': return Vec3( 1.0 if self.x > 0 else (-1.0 if self.x < 0 else 0.0), 1.0 if self.y > 0 else (-1.0 if self.y < 0 else 0.0), 1.0 if self.z > 0 else (-1.0 if self.z < 0 else 0.0)) class IVec3: def init(self, x: int, y: int, z: int): self.x = x self.y = y self.z = z @staticmethod def floor(p: Vec3) -> 'IVec3': return IVec3(math.floor(p.x), math.floor(p.y), math.floor(p.z)) class Ray3hit: def init(self, distance: float, voxel: IVec3, normal: Optional[IVec3]): self.distance = distance self.voxel = voxel self.normal = normal class BoundingVolume3: def init(self, size: Vec3): self.size = size def containspoint(self, voxel: IVec3) -> bool: # Placeholder for actual occupancy check logic # In a real implementation, this would check a sparse data structure return True def testaabbofchunk(volume: BoundingVolume3, frompt: Vec3, direction: Vec3, distance: float) -> Optional[Vec3]: minpt = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) maxpt = volume.size t = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] for i in range(3): diri = direction.x if i == 0 else (direction.y if i == 1 else direction.z) fromi = frompt.x if i == 0 else (frompt.y if i == 1 else frompt.z) mini = minpt.x if i == 0 else (minpt.y if i == 1 else minpt.z) maxi = maxpt.x if i == 0 else (maxpt.y if i == 1 else maxpt.z) if diri > 0.0: t[i] = (mini - fromi) / diri else: t[i] = (maxi - fromi) / diri mi = 0 if t[0] > t[1]: if t[0] > t[2]: mi = 0 else: mi = 2 else: if t[1] > t[2]: mi = 1 else: mi = 2 if t[mi] >= 0.0 and t[mi] <= distance: ptx = frompt.x + direction.x t[mi] pty = frompt.y + direction.y t[mi] ptz = frompt.z + direction.z t[mi] o1 = (mi + 1) % 3 o2 = (mi + 2) % 3 # Check other dimensions if o1 == 1: if not (minpt.y <= pty <= maxpt.y): return None elif o1 == 2: if not (minpt.z <= ptz <= maxpt.z): return None if o2 == 1: if not (minpt.y <= pty <= maxpt.y): return None elif o2 == 2: if not (minpt.z <= ptz <= maxpt.z): return None return Vec3(ptx, pty, ptz) return None class VoxelRay3Iterator: def init(self, volume: BoundingVolume3, p: Vec3, d: Vec3, raylength: float): self.volume = volume self.maxd = 0.0 self.i = IVec3(0, 0, 0) self.step = IVec3(0, 0, 0) self.delta = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) self.dist = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) self.tmax = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) self.t = 0.0 self.norm = None self.done = False dnormalized = d.normalize() t = 0.0 if not volume.containspoint(IVec3.floor(p)): aabb = testaabbofchunk(volume, p, dnormalized, raylength) if aabb is None: self.done = True return aabbpt = aabb p = Vec3(aabbpt.x - dnormalized.x 2.0, aabbpt.y - dnormalized.y 2.0, aabbpt.z - dnormalized.z 2.0) t += (p - aabbpt).length() - 2.0 maxdval = min(raylength, t + Vec3(volume.size.x, volume.size.y, volume.size.z).length() + 2.0) self.maxd = maxdval self.i = IVec3.floor(p) self.step = IVec3( 1 if dnormalized.x > 0 else (-1 if dnormalized.x < 0 else 0), 1 if dnormalized.y > 0 else (-1 if dnormalized.y < 0 else 0), 1 if dnormalized.z > 0 else (-1 if dnormalized.z < 0 else 0)) eps = 1e-7 # f32::EPSILON approximation self.delta = Vec3( float('inf') if abs(dnormalized.x) < eps else 1.0 / abs(dnormalized.x), float('inf') if abs(dnormalized.y) < eps else 1.0 / abs(dnormalized.y), float('inf') if abs(dnormalized.z) < eps else 1.0 / abs(dnormalized.z)) self.dist = Vec3( self.i.x + 1.0 - p.x if self.step.x > 0 else p.x - self.i.x, self.i.y + 1.0 - p.y if self.step.y > 0 else p.y - self.i.y, self.i.z + 1.0 - p.z if self.step.z > 0 else p.z - self.i.z) self.tmax = Vec3( self.delta.x self.dist.x if self.delta.x < float('inf') else float('inf'), self.delta.y self.dist.y if self.delta.y < float('inf') else float('inf'), self.delta.z self.dist.z if self.delta.z < float('inf') else float('inf')) self.t = t def iter(self): return self def next(self) -> Optional[Ray3hit]: if self.done: return None while self.t <= self.maxd: hit = None if self.volume.containspoint(self.i): hit = Ray3hit(self.t, self.i, self.norm) if self.tmax.x < self.tmax.y: if self.tmax.x < self.tmax.z: self.i.x += self.step.x self.t = self.tmax.x self.tmax.x += self.delta.x self.norm = IVec3(-self.step.x, 0, 0) else: self.i.z += self.step.z self.t = self.tmax.z self.tmax.z += self.delta.z self.norm = IVec3(0, 0, -self.step.z) else: if self.tmax.y < self.tmax.z: self.i.y += self.step.y self.t = self.tmax.y self.tmax.y += self.delta.y self.norm = IVec3(0, -self.step.y, 0) else: self.i.z += self.step.z self.t = self.tmax.z self.tmax.z += self.delta.z self.norm = IVec3(0, 0, -self.step.z) if hit is not None: return hit self.done = True return None volume: BoundingVolume3 - The volume being traversed, containing size and containment logic. Zero Direction Component: If a direction component is near zero (|dk| < \epsilon), \deltak is set to \infty to prevent division by zero and correctly handle rays parallel to an axis. Boundary Precision: The initial AABB test backs off the origin by 2.0 units to ensure the ray starts inside the first voxel, preventing missed hits due to floating-point inaccuracies at boundaries. Not given in the sources. The method implements a voxel traversal algorithm using an AABB test, calculates steps, deltas, and tmax values, and iterates through voxels.
