name: NanoVolumeHDDA
head: Span-merging hierarchical DDA, Zero-allocation callback-based HDDA
body: NanoVolumeHDDA is an iterator that traverses a NanoGrid along a ray to yield merged active spans (t0, t1) without heap allocations. It merges adjacent active leaves and tiles to eliminate seam artifacts at 8-voxel tile edges. It builds on Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA) by operating specifically on the NanoGrid structure and optimizing for zero-allocation iteration. Inputs: A NanoGrid (containing the sparse voxel data), a Ray (origin and direction). Outputs: TimeSpan structs representing merged active regions along the ray in front-to-back order, yielded via an iterator protocol that internally invokes a callback. Data Structures: TimeSpan: A struct with fields t0::Float64 and t1::Float64. HDDAState{T}: A mutable struct maintaining traversal state: roots::Vector{Tuple{Float64, Int}}: List of root hits, storing (tmin, offset). rootidx::Int: Current index in the roots list. i2ndda::Union{NodeDDA, Nothing}: The DDA state for the I2 (tile) level. i2off::Int: Offset in the buffer for the current I2 node. i2tentry::Float64: Entry time for the current I2 cell. i1ndda::Union{NodeDDA, Nothing}: The DDA state for the I1 (leaf) level. i1off::Int: Offset in the buffer for the current I1 node. i1tentry::Float64: Entry time for the current I1 cell. spant0::Float64: Start time of the current accumulated span; -1.0 indicates no open span. NodeDDA: Internal state for hierarchical DDA stepping, providing nodeddainside, nodeddachildindex, nodeddacelltime, and step operations. Parameters: MAXROOTS: Maximum number of root nodes to process, set to 8. spant0: -1.0 indicates no open span. Algorithm Steps: 1. Collect Root Hits: Iterate i from 0 to rootcount - 1. Calculate entry pointer ep = rootpos + i entrysz. Load ischild from buffer at ep + 12. If ischild != 0x01, continue to next i. Load i2off from buffer at ep + 13. Load origin from buffer at i2off. Construct an AABB with origin as the center and size 4096.0 (extending to origin + (4096, 4096, 4096)). Intersect ray with this AABB. If the intersection is valid, let hit[1] be the entry time tmin. Store (tmin, i2off) in the roots list. Break if the number of roots exceeds MAXROOTS (8). 2. Sort Roots: Perform an insertion sort on the roots list based on the entry time tmin (first element of the tuple) to ensure front-to-back processing order. 3. Initialize State: If roots is empty, return nothing (no intersection). Initialize HDDAState with the sorted roots, rootidx = 0, i2ndda = nothing, i2off = 0, i2tentry = 0.0, i1ndda = nothing, i1off = 0, i1tentry = 0.0, and spant0 = -1.0. 4. Iterate (Callback Loop): The iteration proceeds by calling an internal advance function hddaadvance which manages two phases. Phase 1: I1 (Leaf) DDA Loop While s.i1ndda is not nothing and nodeddainside(s.i1ndda) is true: Get ndda = s.i1ndda and cidx = nodeddachildindex(ndda). Check haschild by testing if the child mask bit cidx is set at s.i1off + I1CMASKOFF in the buffer. Check hastile: If !haschild, check if the voxel mask bit cidx is set at s.i1off + I1VMASKOFF. If haschild or hastile is true AND s.spant0 < 0.0: Set s.spant0 = s.i1tentry. If !(haschild or hastile) is true AND s.spant0 >= 0.0: Call the callback f(s.spant0, s.i1tentry). Reset s.spant0 = -1.0. Update s.i1tentry = nodeddacelltime(ndda). Step ndda.state. Phase 2: I2 (Tile) DDA Loop After Phase 1 (or if Phase 1 was not entered), loop while s.i2ndda is not nothing and nodeddainside(s.i2ndda) is true: Get ndda = s.i2ndda and cidx = nodeddachildindex(ndda). Check haschild by testing if the child mask bit cidx is set at s.i2off + I2CMASKOFF in the buffer. If haschild is true: Calculate tidx using bufcountonbefore to determine the child index count. Load i1off for the child node. Construct an I1 AABB with size 128.0 centered at the child's origin. Intersect ray with this I1 AABB. If it hits: Initialize s.i1ndda with nodeddainit(ray, tmin, i1origin, Int32(16), Int32(8)). Set s.i1tentry = tmin. Set s.i1off = i1off. continue to the I2 loop (which will re-enter Phase 1 in the next advance call). If I1 AABB misses: If s.spant0 >= 0.0, call f(s.spant0, s.i2tentry) and reset s.spant0 = -1.0. If haschild is false: Check hastile by testing if the voxel mask bit cidx is set at s.i2off + I2VMASKOFF. If hastile is true AND s.spant0 < 0.0: Set s.spant0 = s.i2tentry. If !hastile is true AND s.spant0 >= 0.0: Call f(s.spant0, s.i2tentry) and reset s.spant0 = -1.0. Update s.i2tentry = nodeddacelltime(ndda). Step ndda.state. Finalization: After the I2 loop exhausts, if s.spant0 >= 0.0, call f(s.spant0, s.i2tentry) and reset s.spant0 = -1.0. Return the next span or nothing if traversal is complete. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def nanovolumehddaiterate(grid, ray, callback): """ Iterates over a NanoGrid along a ray, yielding merged active spans via callback. """ # 1. Collect Root Hits roots = [] rootcount = grid.rootcount rootpos = grid.rootbufferptr entrysz = grid.rootentrysize # Typically 16 bytes based on offsets for i in range(rootcount): ep = rootpos + i entrysz ischild = readbyte(ep + 12) if ischild != 0x01: continue i2off = readint(ep + 13) origin = readvec3(i2off) # AABB: center origin, size 4096.0 aabbmin = origin - vec3(2048.0) aabbmax = origin + vec3(2048.0) hit = intersectbbox(ray, aabbmin, aabbmax) if hit is not None: tmin = hit.entrytime roots.append((tmin, i2off)) if len(roots) >= 8: # MAXROOTS break # 2. Sort Roots (Insertion Sort) for i in range(1, len(roots)): j = i while j > 0 and roots[j][0] < roots[j-1][0]: roots[j], roots[j-1] = roots[j-1], roots[j] j -= 1 if not roots: return # 3. Initialize State state = { 'roots': roots, 'rootidx': 0, 'i2ndda': None, 'i2off': 0, 'i2tentry': 0.0, 'i1ndda': None, 'i1off': 0, 'i1tentry': 0.0, 'spant0': -1.0 } # 4. Iterate while True: span, state = hddaadvance(grid, ray, state) if span is None: break callback(span.t0, span.t1) def hddaadvance(grid, ray, s): buf = grid.buffer # Phase 1: I1 (Leaf) DDA while s['i1ndda'] is not None and nodeddainside(s['i1ndda']): ndda = s['i1ndda'] cidx = nodeddachildindex(ndda) # Check haschild haschild = bufmaskison(buf, s['i1off'] + I1CMASKOFF, cidx) # Check hastile hastile = (not haschild) and bufmaskison(buf, s['i1off'] + I1VMASKOFF, cidx) if (haschild or hastile) and s['spant0'] < 0.0: s['spant0'] = s['i1tentry'] if not (haschild or hastile) and s['spant0'] >= 0.0: span = TimeSpan(s['spant0'], s['i1tentry']) s['spant0'] = -1.0 s['i1tentry'] = nodeddacelltime(ndda) stepndda(ndda) return span, s s['i1tentry'] = nodeddacelltime(ndda) stepndda(ndda) s['i1ndda'] = None # Phase 2: I2 (Tile) DDA while s['i2ndda'] is not None and nodeddainside(s['i2ndda']): ndda = s['i2ndda'] cidx = nodeddachildindex(ndda) haschild = bufmaskison(buf, s['i2off'] + I2CMASKOFF, cidx) if haschild: tidx = bufcountonbefore(buf, s['i2off'] + I2CMASKOFF, cidx) i1off = getchildoffset(buf, s['i2off'], tidx) i1origin = getnodeorigin(buf, i1off) # I1 AABB: center i1origin, size 128.0 aabbmin = i1origin - vec3(64.0) aabbmax = i1origin + vec3(64.0) hit = intersectbbox(ray, aabbmin, aabbmax) if hit is not None: tmin = hit.entrytime s['i1ndda'] = nodeddainit(ray, tmin, i1origin, 16, 8) s['i1tentry'] = tmin s['i1off'] = i1off # Continue to I2 loop to re-enter Phase 1 in next advance return None, s else: # I1 Miss if s['spant0'] >= 0.0: span = TimeSpan(s['spant0'], s['i2tentry']) s['spant0'] = -1.0 return span, s else: hastile = bufmaskison(buf, s['i2off'] + I2VMASKOFF, cidx) if hastile and s['spant0'] < 0.0: s['spant0'] = s['i2tentry'] elif not hastile and s['spant0'] >= 0.0: span = TimeSpan(s['spant0'], s['i2tentry']) s['spant0'] = -1.0 return span, s s['i2tentry'] = nodeddacelltime(ndda) stepndda(ndda) # I2 Exhausted if s['spant0'] >= 0.0: span = TimeSpan(s['spant0'], s['i2tentry']) s['spant0'] = -1.0 return span, s return None, s def readbyte(addr): return buf[addr] def readint(addr): return buf[addr:addr+4] def readvec3(addr): return vec3(buf[addr], buf[addr+4], buf[addr+8]) def intersectbbox(ray, min, max): # Standard slab intersection; returns hit object with entrytime or None pass def nodeddainside(ndda): return ndda.t < ndda.tmax def nodeddachildindex(ndda): return ndda.cidx def bufmaskison(buf, maskaddr, cidx): return (buf[maskaddr] >> cidx) & 1 def nodeddacelltime(ndda): return ndda.t def stepndda(ndda): ndda.t += ndda.step; ndda.cidx += 1 def bufcountonbefore(buf, maskaddr, cidx): return sum(1 for i in range(cidx) if (buf[maskaddr] >> i) & 1) def getchildoffset(buf, parentoff, tidx): return parentoff + tidx childstride def getnodeorigin(buf, off): return readvec3(off) Time Complexity: Not given in the sources. Memory Complexity: O(1) auxiliary memory per ray traversal instance, as it avoids heap allocations for span lists. Strengths: Zero-allocation iteration makes it suitable for GPU kernels or high-performance CPU loops where memory fragmentation or GC pressure is a concern. Merging spans reduces the number of shader invocations. Limitations: Bounded root count (8) may miss intersections in highly fragmented scenes if not handled by the caller. Specific to NanoGrid structure. When to use: When rendering sparse voxel grids (VDB) with NanoGrid and performance/zero-allocation is critical. When not to use: For dense grids where linear traversal might be faster, or if the grid structure does not support the NanoGrid format. NanoVolumeHDDA is part of the Lyr.jl rendering library, developed by Tobias Osborne. It is designed to efficiently traverse sparse voxel data structures (specifically NanoGrid) for volume rendering, leveraging the hierarchical nature of the data to skip empty space and merge active regions. tobiasosborne/Lyr.jl, https://github.com/tobiasosborne/Lyr.jl, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)

name: RayMajorantIterator
head: HDDA-based ray traversal for volume majorant
body: The RayMajorantIterator is an iterator that traverses a sparse volume grid using a Hybrid Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA) to step through voxels or leaves, computing the maximum density (majorant) for each segment where the majorant remains constant. It solves the problem of efficiently determining integration segments for volume path tracing by avoiding per-voxel sampling in empty or uniform regions. It builds on Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA) by bundling consecutive steps with identical majorants into single segments, reducing overhead compared to standard voxel DDA which cannot skip inactive nodes or handle variable leaf sizes efficiently. Inputs and Outputs: Input: A ray (RayT), a grid accessor (const GridT::AccessorType&), and an optional debug buffer (std::vector<DDAStep>). Output: A sequence of Segment structs, each containing start time t0, end time t1, and the constant majorant density dmaj for that segment. Data Structures: The iterator maintains the following state fields: float mscale: Inverse of the ray direction length in index space, calculated as 1 / density.worldToIndexDirF(ray.dir()).length(). RayT mray: The ray object (typically nanovdb::math::Ray<float>). float mmajorant: The current segment's majorant density, initialized to std::numericlimits<float>::signalingNaN(). const GridT::AccessorType& macc: Reference to the grid accessor for probing values. nanovdb::math::HDDA<RayT> mdda: The HDDA instance managing the traversal step. std::vector<DDAStep> msteprecorddst: Pointer to a debug buffer for recording step details. The Segment struct returned by the iterator contains: float t0: Start time in voxel units. float t1: End time in voxel units. float dmaj: Majorant density value for the segment. The DDAStep struct (used for debugging) contains: int dim: HDDA dimension stepped. float majorant: Current majorant. float t: Current time. Eigen::Vector3i voxel: Current voxel coordinates. Eigen::Vector3f hit: World position. Algorithm Steps: 1. Initialization: Calculate mscale = 1.0f / density.worldToIndexDirF(mray.dir()).length(). Initialize mmajorant to std::numericlimits<float>::signalingNaN(). Initialize mdda with the ray and an initial dimension. The initial dimension is determined by gethddadim, which returns std::max<uint32t>(8, acc.getDim(ijk, ray)). This ensures a minimum step dimension of 8 to avoid skipping active leaves. 2. Iteration (next() method): Termination Check: If mdda.time() >= mdda.maxTime(), the ray has left the bounding box. Return std::nullopt. Start Time: Set ans.t0 = mdda.time(). Majorant Update: If mmajorant is NaN, call updatecurrentmajorant() and recordstep(). Dimension Update: Calculate the new HDDA dimension for the next step using the coordinate mray(mdda.time() + 1.0001f).floor(). The offset 1.0001f ensures the coordinate is slightly ahead of the current step to get the correct dimension for the next step, preventing issues with pessimistic HDDA stepping in empty space. Update mdda with mdda.update(mray, newdim). Loop for Constant Majorant: Call updatecurrentmajorant() and recordstep(). If the new mmajorant equals ans.dmaj (the majorant of the current segment), continue the loop to bundle this step into the current segment. If mmajorant differs, exit the loop. End Time: Set ans.t1 = mdda.time(). Return: Return the Segment struct with t0, t1, and dmaj. 3. Majorant Calculation (updatecurrentmajorant()): Determine the current voxel index ijk from the HDDA state. If the current node is not a leaf, attempt to probe the value using macc.probeValue(ijk, value). If probeValue returns true, set mmajorant = value and return. Otherwise, set mmajorant = 0.0f (empty space). Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math from typing import Optional, Tuple, List class RayMajorantIterator: def init(self, ray, accessor, debugbuffer: Optional[List] = None): self.mray = ray self.macc = accessor self.msteprecorddst = debugbuffer # mscale = 1 / density.worldToIndexDirF(ray.dir()).length() self.mscale = 1.0 / ray.dir().length() self.mmajorant = float('nan') # Initial dimension calculation ensures minimum step of 8 ijkinitial = ray.time(0).floor().astype(int) initdim = max(8, accessor.getDim(ijkinitial, ray)) # HDDA state management and stepping logic are handled by the parent nanovdb::math::HDDA library. self.mdda = HDDA(ray, initdim) def gethddadim(self, ijk, ray, accessor): return max(8, accessor.getDim(ijk, ray)) def updatecurrentmajorant(self): ijk = self.mdda.getvoxelindex() # probeValue returns (success, value) success, value = self.macc.probeValue(ijk) if success: self.mmajorant = value else: self.mmajorant = 0.0 def recordstep(self): if self.msteprecorddst is not None: step = DDAStep( dim=self.mdda.getdim(), majorant=self.mmajorant, t=self.mdda.time(), voxel=self.mdda.getvoxelindex(), hit=self.mray.time(self.mdda.time())) self.msteprecorddst.append(step) def next(self) -> Optional[Tuple[float, float, float]]: if self.mdda.time() >= self.mdda.maxtime(): return None anst0 = self.mdda.time() if math.isnan(self.mmajorant): self.updatecurrentmajorant() self.recordstep() ansdmaj = self.mmajorant while True: nexttimeapprox = self.mdda.time() + 1.0001 ijknext = self.mray.time(nexttimeapprox).floor().astype(int) newdim = self.gethddadim(ijknext, self.mray, self.macc) self.mdda.update(self.mray, newdim) self.updatecurrentmajorant() self.recordstep() if self.mmajorant != ansdmaj: break if self.mdda.time() >= self.mdda.maxtime(): break anst1 = self.mdda.time() return (anst0, anst1, ansdmaj) class HDDA: def init(self, ray, dim): self.ray = ray self.dim = dim self.currenttime = 0.0 self.maxtime = 1000.0 # Bounding box max time not given in sources def time(self): return self.currenttime def maxtime(self): return self.maxtime def update(self, ray, dim): self.currenttime += 1.0 / ray.dir().length() self.dim = dim def getvoxelindex(self): pos = self.ray.time(self.currenttime) return pos.floor().astype(int) def getdim(self): return self.dim class DDAStep: def init(self, dim, majorant, t, voxel, hit): self.dim = dim self.majorant = majorant self.t = t self.voxel = voxel self.hit = hit Parameters and Typical Values: Minimum HDDA Dimension: 8. This is hardcoded to avoid skipping active leaves in sparse grids. Time Offset for Dimension Update: 1.0001f. This small epsilon ensures the coordinate used for dimension lookup is slightly ahead of the current step, handling pessimistic HDDA stepping in empty space. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Pessimistic HDDA Stepping: HDDA stepping can be pessimistic in empty space, potentially stepping more frequently than necessary. The iterator mitigates this by bundling consecutive segments with the same majorant into one, reducing overhead. Boundary Conditions: The termination check mdda.time() >= mdda.maxTime() handles the case where the ray leaves the bounding box. Precision: The use of 1.0001f offset is critical for correct dimension updates. Using 1.0f might result in the same voxel being queried, leading to incorrect dimension updates or infinite loops in degenerate cases. Time Complexity: The iterator steps through the grid using HDDA, which allows skipping inactive nodes. The complexity is proportional to the number of distinct majorant segments along the ray, which is typically much less than the number of voxels intersected, especially in sparse or uniform regions. Memory Complexity: The iterator maintains a small constant amount of state per ray (HDDA state, current majorant, etc.). The debug buffer, if used, scales with the number of steps. Strengths: Efficiently handles sparse voxel grids by skipping empty space and variable leaf sizes. Bundling segments with the same majorant reduces the number of integration steps required for volume path tracing. Limitations: HDDA stepping can be pessimistic in empty space, although this is mitigated by segment bundling. The method relies on the underlying HDDA implementation's correctness and efficiency. When to Use: Ideal for volume path tracing in sparse voxel grids where empty space is common and majorant values are constant over large segments. When Not to Use: If the volume is dense and majorant values change frequently per voxel, the overhead of HDDA and segment bundling might not provide significant benefits over standard voxel DDA. The RayMajorantIterator is part of the volume path tracer developed by Shibodd. It leverages the NanoVDB library's HDDA implementation for efficient hierarchical traversal. The method was designed to optimize volume rendering by reducing the number of samples required for accurate integration, particularly in large, sparse scenes. Shibodd/volumepathtracer, https://github.com/Shibodd/volumepathtracer, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)

name: HDDA Hybrid
body: HDDA Hybrid is a ray traversal algorithm for sparse voxel grids that combines hierarchical skipping with fine-grained traversal. It uses Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA) to skip empty tiles at resolutions coarser than the leaf level, and switches to standard Digital Differential Analyzer (DDA) to traverse occupied tiles voxel-by-voxel. This approach avoids per-voxel checks in empty space while maintaining sampling accuracy in dense regions. It builds on Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA). Inputs: Ray origin \mathbf{o} and direction \mathbf{d}, ray bounds t{min}, t{max}, VDB grid accessor acc providing isActive(ijk), getDim(ijk, ray), and root bounding box, leafdim (typically 8), coneangle (default 0.0), stepsize (default 10^{-3}), and firstpass flag. Outputs: A sequence of sample points (t, \mathbf{x}) along the ray within occupied regions. Data Structures: hdda (tile traversal state), dda (voxel traversal state), tlast (last processed time), ntrav (voxel counter). Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def traversehddahybrid(ray, acc, leafdim, coneangle, stepsize, firstpass): t0 = ray.t0() + 1e-6 t1 = ray.t1() - 1e-6 if not ray.clip(acc.root().bbox()) or t0 >= t1: return [] ijk = rounddown(ray(t0)) dim = acc.getdim(ijk, ray) tilemode = dim >= leafdim hdda.init(ray, t0, t1, max(leafdim, dim)) ddaIsValid = True tlast = t0 ntrav = 0 samples = [] while ddaIsValid and hdda.time() <= hdda.next(): if not ddaIsValid: dda.init(ray, hdda.time(), hdda.next()) tlast = advancetime(tlast, coneangle, stepsize, hdda.time()) ddaIsValid = True while ddaIsValid: dt = calcdt(tlast, coneangle, stepsize, 1e10) active = acc.isActive(dda.voxel()) while tlast + dt / 2 < dda.next(): if active: if not firstpass: samples.append((tlast + dt / 2, ray(tlast + dt / 2))) ntrav += 1 tlast += dt dt = calcdt(tlast, coneangle, stepsize, 1e10) else: tlast += dt ddaIsValid = dda.step() ddaIsValid = hdda.step() ijk = hdda.voxel() dim = acc.getdim(ijk, ray) tilemode = dim >= leafdim hdda.update(ray, max(leafdim, dim)) return samples def calcdt(tlast, coneangle, stepsize, maxdt): return min(stepsize (1 + coneangle tlast), maxdt) def advancetime(tlast, coneangle, stepsize, nextt): return max(tlast, nextt) # Parameters: leafdim = 8, coneangle = 0.0, stepsize = 10^{-3}. Edge Cases: Epsilon offset (10^{-6}) in t0, t1 prevents boundary precision errors. Degenerate rays (t0 \ge t1) are skipped immediately. HDDA Skip is a ray traversal algorithm for sparse voxel grids (such as VDB) that uses Hierarchical DDA to skip empty regions in bulk steps, advancing ray time t rather than sampling every voxel. It builds on HDDA Hybrid, which combines HDDA for empty tiles and DDA for occupied tiles; HDDA Skip extends this by allowing density-based skipping of invisible space within occupied regions using optional \sigma or \alpha functions. Optimized for very small volumes or specific hardware constraints. Choose when memory footprint is critical. Uses a majorant function to skip empty space. Choose when a tight majorant is available and HDDA overhead is too high. Time Complexity: Not given in the sources. Memory Complexity: Not given in the sources. Performance: Faster than pure DDA in sparse scenes due to skipping empty tiles, but slower than HDDA Skip when sampling is required due to DDA switching overhead. Strengths: Efficient for sparse voxel grids with mixed density. Limitations: Overhead of managing two traversal states. When to use: Sparse voxel NeRF rendering, VDB-based volume visualization. When not to use: Fully dense volumes, or when only occupancy queries are needed (use HDDA Skip). HDDA Hybrid was introduced in the context of accelerating occupancy grid-based NeRF rendering using VDB grids. It was presented by Yoshihiro Kato et al. in "Plug-and-Play Acceleration of Occupancy Grid-based NeRF Rendering using VDB Grid and Hierarchical Ray Traversal" (2024). The method leverages the B+tree structure of VDB to perform multi-resolution leapfrogging, combining the coarse skipping of HDDA with the precision of DDA. name: HDDA Skip
head: Hierarchical DDA (HDDA) Skip
body: HDDA Skip is a ray traversal algorithm for sparse voxel grids (such as VDB) that uses Hierarchical DDA to skip empty regions in bulk steps, advancing ray time t rather than sampling every voxel. It builds on HDDA Hybrid, which combines HDDA for empty tiles and DDA for occupied tiles; HDDA Skip extends this by allowing density-based skipping of invisible space within occupied regions using optional \sigma or \alpha functions. Inputs: Ray origins \mathbf{o}, normalized directions \mathbf{d}, grid bounds [t0, t1], optional density/opacity functions \sigma(\cdot) or \alpha(\cdot), step size s, cone angle \theta, and grid accessors for voxel activity and dimension. Outputs: Sampled points (t{left}, t{right}), ray indices, and traversal counts. Data Structures: HDDAState: Stores current voxel index \mathbf{ijk}, dimension dim, current time t, and validity flag. Ray: Origin \mathbf{o}, direction \mathbf{d}, bounds t{min}, t{max}. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def hddaskiptraverse(ray, acc, firstpass=True): # 1. Initialize bounds t0 = ray.t0() + 1e-6 t1 = ray.t1() - 1e-6 if not ray.clip(acc.root().bbox()) or t0 > t1: return # Skip to next grid # 2. Initialize HDDA state ijk = floor(ray(t0)) # nanovdb::RoundDown dim = acc.getDim(ijk, ray) hdda.init(ray, t0, t1, dim) ddaIsValid = True tlast = t0 # tlast initialized to t0 # 3. Outer loop while ddaIsValid: # Inner skip loop while ddaIsValid and not acc.isActive(ijk): ddaIsValid = hdda.step() if not ddaIsValid: break ijk = hdda.voxel() dim = acc.getDim(ijk, ray) hdda.update(ray, dim) # 4. Advance to occupied region if not ddaIsValid: break tlast = advancetime(tlast, ray.coneangle, ray.stepsize, hdda.time()) # 5. Traverse occupied region dt = calcdt(tlast, ray.coneangle, ray.stepsize, 1e10) while tlast + dt / 2 < hdda.next(): if not firstpass: recordsample(rayindices, tlast, tlast + dt) ntrav += 1 tlast += dt dt = calcdt(tlast, ray.coneangle, ray.stepsize, 1e10) # 6. Step HDDA for next iteration ddaIsValid = hdda.step() ijk = hdda.voxel() dim = acc.getDim(ijk, ray) hdda.update(ray, dim) Note: advancetime and calcdt are internal helper functions; their exact implementations are not provided in the sources. Formulas: t0 = \text{ray.t0()} + 10^{-6} t1 = \text{ray.t1()} - 10^{-6} \mathbf{ijk} = \lfloor \mathbf{o} + t0 \mathbf{d} \rfloor dt = \text{calc\dt}(t{last}, \theta, s, 10^{10}) Parameters: renderstepsize: Default 10^{-3}. coneangle: Default 0.0. earlystopeps: Default 10^{-4}. alphathre: Default 0.0. Edge Cases: Ray bounds invalid (t0 > t1): Skip grid. Empty grid: HDDA becomes invalid immediately. Precision: Use \epsilon = 10^{-6} to avoid boundary issues. Time Complexity: Proportional to number of occupied voxels traversed, plus overhead of HDDA steps for empty regions. Memory Complexity: O(1) per ray for traversal state. Strengths: Efficiently skips large empty regions; supports density-based early termination. Limitations: Requires active voxel check; density evaluation adds overhead if used. When to Use: Sparse grids with large empty regions; when density-based skipping is beneficial. When Not to Use: Dense grids where overhead of HDDA outweighs benefits; when no density function is available and simple DDA is sufficient. Originated in the faster-occgrid project by Yosshi999, HDDA Skip is an unofficial implementation leveraging Hierarchical DDA for efficient traversal of sparse voxel grids. It extends the HDDA Hybrid approach by integrating density-based skipping capabilities. Yosshi999/faster-occgrid, https://github.com/Yosshi999/faster-occgrid, fetched 2026-10-24 (unofficial)

name: VolumeHDDA
head: Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer for Volume, Volume Hierarchical DDA (VolumeHDDA), VolumeHDDA (Hierarchical DDA for Volumes), VolumeHDDA< TreeT, RayT, 0 >, ChildLevel>, ChildNodeLevel>
body: VolumeHDDA is a specialized Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA) designed for ray intersections against generic volume trees. It traverses from a specified ChildNodeLevel down to the leaf level (specialized at 0), performing hierarchical ray-marching by entering child nodes when present and processing active/inactive tiles at leaf levels. It sets itself apart from its sibling Hierarchical Digital Differential Analyzer (HDDA) by being explicitly templated for volume tree structures (handling TreeT, RayT, and ChildNodeLevel) and managing time spans for active/inactive tile sequences, whereas the generic HDDA focuses on geometric intersection tests. Inputs and Outputs: Inputs: A RayT object (representing the ray with methods valid(), setTimes(t0, t1), invDir(), operator()(time)), an AccessorT object (providing probeConstNode<NodeT>(coord) and isValueOn(coord)), and a TimeSpanT object t (tracking the current active segment, initialized to (-1, -1)). Outputs: For march, a TimeSpanT representing the first continuous active segment or (-1, -1) if none. For hits, a list of TimeSpanT intervals collected into ListT. Data Structures: The class VolumeHDDA<TreeT, RayT, int ChildNodeLevel> contains: math::DDA<RayT, NodeT::TOTAL> mDDA: A DDA instance for the current node level. NodeT is defined as typename ChainT::template Get<ChildNodeLevel>, where ChainT is typename TreeT::RootNodeType::NodeChainType. VolumeHDDA<TreeT, RayT, ChildNodeLevel-1> mHDDA: A recursive instance for the next lower level. Parameters: TreeT: The tree type being traversed. RayT: The ray type used for traversal. ChildNodeLevel: Template argument specifying the entry upper node level for hierarchical ray-marching. The final lowest level is always the leaf node level (specialized at 0), not the voxel level. LeafT: Defined as typename TreeT::LeafNodeType. TimeSpanT: Defined as typename RayT::TimeSpan. Algorithm Steps: The traversal uses a recursive descent. The general case (for ChildNodeLevel > 0) and the base case (ChildNodeLevel == 0) share similar logic but differ in node probing. 1. Initialization: Initialize mDDA with the ray. In the base case specialization, mDDA is initialized with LeafT::TOTAL. 2. Loop: Iterate using mDDA.step(). Child Node Check: General Case: If acc.probeConstNode<NodeT>(mDDA.voxel()) is not nullptr. Base Case: If acc.probeConstNode<LeafT>(mDDA.voxel()) is not nullptr OR acc.isValueOn(mDDA.voxel()). Action: Set ray times to (mDDA.time(), mDDA.next()). Recursively call mHDDA.march (or hits). If the recursive call returns true (for march) or collects data (for hits), handle termination/collection and continue or return. Active Tile Check: If acc.isValueOn(mDDA.voxel()) is true: If t.t0 < 0: Set t.t0 = mDDA.time(). Inactive Tile / Segment Closure: If t.t0 >= 0 (an active segment is open) and the current tile is inactive (or the child node check failed and we are in an inactive region): Set t.t1 = mDDA.time(). If t.valid() (both t0 and t1 are set): For march: Return true. For hits: Push t to times. Reset t.set(-1, -1). 3. Termination: After the loop, if t.t0 >= 0 (the ray ended while in an active segment), set t.t1 = mDDA.maxTime(). Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. class VolumeHDDA: def init(self, TreeT, RayT, ChildNodeLevel): self.mDDA = DDA(RayT, NodeT.TOTAL) self.mHDDA = VolumeHDDA(TreeT, RayT, ChildNodeLevel - 1) self.NodeT = ChainT.Get(ChildNodeLevel) def march(self, ray, acc): t = TimeSpanT(-1, -1) if ray.valid(): self.marchrecursive(ray, acc, t) return t def marchrecursive(self, ray, acc, t): self.mDDA.init(ray) while True: voxel = self.mDDA.voxel() # Check for child node if acc.probeConstNode(self.NodeT, voxel) is not None: ray.setTimes(self.mDDA.time(), self.mDDA.next()) if self.mHDDA.marchrecursive(ray, acc, t): return True # Check for active tile elif acc.isValueOn(voxel): if t.t0 < 0: t.t0 = self.mDDA.time() # Check for inactive tile closing an active segment elif t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.time() if t.valid(): return True t.set(-1, -1) if not self.mDDA.step(): break if t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.maxTime() return False def hits(self, ray, acc, times, t): self.mDDA.init(ray) while True: voxel = self.mDDA.voxel() if acc.probeConstNode(self.NodeT, voxel) is not None: ray.setTimes(self.mDDA.time(), self.mDDA.next()) self.mHDDA.hits(ray, acc, times, t) elif acc.isValueOn(voxel): if t.t0 < 0: t.t0 = self.mDDA.time() elif t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.time() if t.valid(): times.pushback(t) t.set(-1, -1) if not self.mDDA.step(): break if t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.maxTime() class VolumeHDDALeaf: def init(self, TreeT, RayT): self.mDDA = DDA(RayT, LeafT.TOTAL) self.LeafT = TreeT.LeafNodeType def march(self, ray, acc): t = TimeSpanT(-1, -1) if ray.valid(): self.marchrecursive(ray, acc, t) return t def marchrecursive(self, ray, acc, t): self.mDDA.init(ray) while True: voxel = self.mDDA.voxel() # Check for leaf node or active tile if acc.probeConstNode(self.LeafT, voxel) is not None or acc.isValueOn(voxel): if t.t0 < 0: t.t0 = self.mDDA.time() # Check for inactive tile closing an active segment elif t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.time() if t.valid(): return True t.set(-1, -1) if not self.mDDA.step(): break if t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.maxTime() return False def hits(self, ray, acc, times, t): self.mDDA.init(ray) while True: voxel = self.mDDA.voxel() if acc.probeConstNode(self.LeafT, voxel) is not None or acc.isValueOn(voxel): if t.t0 < 0: t.t0 = self.mDDA.time() elif t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.time() if t.valid(): times.pushback(t) t.set(-1, -1) if not self.mDDA.step(): break if t.t0 >= 0: t.t1 = self.mDDA.maxTime() Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Time Span Management: The TimeSpanT t is initialized to (-1, -1). t.t0 marks the start of an active segment, t.t1 marks the end. If an inactive tile is hit after an active segment, the segment is closed. If the ray ends while still in an active segment (t.t0 >= 0 after loop), t.t1 is set to maxTime. Precision: The DDA relies on floating-point arithmetic for ray parameterization. Precision issues may arise with very long rays or small nodes, though the DDA implementation typically handles this via clamping. Boundaries: The ray must be valid (ray.valid()) before traversal. If the ray does not intersect the volume bounds, the loop may not execute or return immediately. A reorganization of Hierarchical Data-Driven Approach (HDDA) iterators that separates the traversal of all active values from the traversal of only leaf voxels, enabling tile-skipping for leaf-specific operations. It sets itself apart from its parent VolumeHDDA by providing a specialized leaf-only traversal path that avoids processing active coarse tiles, addressing the latent mis-indexing bugs that occurred when callers assumed the previous single iterator yielded only leaf voxels. Time Complexity: Proportional to the number of nodes visited along the ray path, skipping inactive subtrees. The hierarchical nature reduces the number of visited nodes compared to linear traversal, especially for sparse volumes. Memory Complexity: Low, as it uses recursion and does not store the entire traversal path. The stack depth is proportional to the tree depth. Strengths: Efficient for sparse volumes due to hierarchical skipping. Handles active/inactive tile sequences correctly. Limitations: Overhead of recursive calls and template instantiation. Performance depends on the tree structure and ray direction. When to use: When traversing volume trees for ray-marching or intersection tests, especially when dealing with sparse data or needing to skip inactive regions. When not to use: For dense volumes where linear traversal might be simpler or for non-tree-based volume representations. VolumeHDDA is part of the OpenVDB library, developed by DreamWorks Animation and later by the Academy Software Foundation. It is designed for efficient storage and manipulation of large volumetric datasets, commonly used in visual effects and scientific visualization. The class is defined in openvdb/math/DDA.h.
